newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-GPT sees 9.3 cent 2nd half distrib..
newsitem.headline: RTRS-GPT sees 9.3 cent 2nd half distrib..

text.p: General Property Trust (GPT) said on Thursday it expected a lower distribution of 9.3 cents per unit for the next six months compared with 10.4 cents in the first half to June 30 due to lower retail property income growth.
"We currently forecast distributions for the next six months to be 9.3 cents per unit," GPT said in a statement accompanying its half year results.
GPT paid a first half distribution of 10.4 cents per unit.
GPT reported a A$110.9 million net profit for the six months ended June 30 compared with A$68.1 million a year earlier.
It said that in the office property portfolio, improving market conditions and the leasing of vacant space had delivered higher income returns. "This is expected to continue," it said.
GPT has more than 50 percent of its office portfolio weighting in the Sydney central business district.

GPT said investment markets are currently experiencing a cyclical low in the interest rate cycle. "As a result any further borrowings by GPT are more likely to be medium to long term debt rather than short term debt," GPT said.
"The gearing level of the trust means that GPT is well positioned to meet its future capital expenditure needs and make further acquisitions if appropriate," it said.
GPT said it had about A$150 million still to be raised from the remaining call option under the GPT Options. The exercise date for this last call option must be before June 30, 1998.
GPT's current borrowing ratio is 11 percent, well within the trust deed of 25 percent, GPT said.
GPT units closed 4.7 cents lower at A$2.68 on Wednesday.
